own_solution.law: RC charging: V_C(t) = E (1 - exp(-t/RC)), tau = RC = 20e-6 F * 5000 ohm = 0.1 s
assumptions: capacitor initially uncharged (NOT stated in the problem)
ideal battery with no internal resistance

T8E15.regime: matters only if the asked time is at or after 500 ms; 80 ms < 500 ms so charging is unaffected

T008B.regime: matters only if the asked time is at or after 500 ms; 80 ms < 500 ms so charging is unaffected

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: The problem never states that the capacitor is initially uncharged; with an initial charge V0 the answer becomes 12 - (12 - V0) exp(-0.8), so the initial condition that decides the answer is missing.

counterexamples: If the capacitor starts at 5 V, V_C(80 ms) = 12 - 7*0.4493 = 8.855 V instead of 6.608 V.
notes: Base: tau = 0.1 s, V = 12(1 - e^-0.8) = 12*0.55067 = 6.608 V. With an extra 2 kOhm in series: tau = 0.14 s, V = 12(1 - e^-0.5714) = 12*0.43528 = 5.223 V. Paired sentences state consistent values (all resistor sentences 2 kOhm; both disconnection sentences 500 ms). Minor wording: 'broken again' in T8E15 implies a previous break that was never described (low-level awkwardness only).
